description.p: Ether is a simple desktop client for OpenVPN. Import the .ovpn profile from your OpenVPN server and connect with one click.

ul.li: Big, clear connection status with VPN address, server and traffic
System tray icon for quick connect and disconnect
Optional saved password in your desktop keyring for automatic sign-in
Two-factor authentication, including crtext on OpenVPN 2.5 and newer
Import several profiles at once and search the list
English and Russian, dark and light themes
Connection log in its own window
Updates itself from inside the app

description.p: Needs OpenVPN 2.4 or newer installed on the system (sudo apt install openvpn).

Renames the app to Ether and gives it the EtherOS look: a coral shield icon, a coral window frame with a title bar of its own, flat cards with hairline borders, Adwaita Sans for text and JetBrains Mono for the technical details, and a status card built around the connection state. Connected is coral, connecting is yellow, a failure is red.

Adds profiles dropped onto the window, pasted from the clipboard or downloaded from a link, renaming, a download-speed graph, desktop notifications, automatic reconnection, start with the session, connect on launch, a theme that follows the system, a filterable log with warnings and errors highlighted, a diagnostics button, keyboard shortcuts, and a warning when a profile runs programs as root.

Adds two-factor authentication for static challenges, CRV1 and crtext, so servers that ask for a code now connect. Imports several .ovpn files at once and skips the ones already in the list, adds a profile search, an English and Russian interface, and a dark and light theme.

Fixes connections failing right after sign-in on Arch, Fedora and other distros when a profile asks for the Debian-only group nogroup. Also shows the Ether icon on Wayland, makes links easier to read in dark mode and gives long profile names more room.
Adds an .rpm package for Fedora and openSUSE. File dialogs no longer freeze the window, removing a profile asks for confirmation, and buttons and links work from the keyboard and with screen readers.
States the supported OpenVPN version (2.4 or newer) and drops gateway-specific wording.
